name: H3D
description: Automated semantic segmentation and object detection are of great importance in geospatial data analysis. However, supervised machine learning systems such as convolutional neural networks require large corpora of annotated training data. Especially in the geospatial domain, such datasets are quite scarce. Within this paper, we aim to alleviate this issue by introducing a new annotated 3D dataset that is unique in three ways: i) The dataset consists of both an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) laser scanning point cloud and a 3D textured mesh. ii) The point cloud features a mean point density of about 800 pts/sqm and the oblique imagery used for 3D mesh texturing realizes a ground sampling distance of about 2-3 cm. This enables the identification of fine-grained structures and represents the state of the art in UAV-based mapping. iii) Both data modalities will be published for a total of three epochs allowing applications such as change detection. The dataset depicts the village of Hessigh
evaluation_method: IoU/F1 and detection metrics such as precision/recall
reputation: A well-known geospatial 3D benchmark in the remote-sensing and UAV mapping community, often used for segmentation and change-detection research.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; relatively specialized and dataset-specific, with performance sensitive to 3D modality choice and temporal split.
